themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge in East New York
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 36 this week versus a baseline of 5.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 602% increase (z-score: 6.76)—suggesting a sudden outbreak of vandalism across CD 305 that warrants investigation into whether this reflects organized tagging, gang activity, or neglected enforcement.
evidence: 36 graffiti complaints last week vs. 5.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (602% spike)
Z-score of 6.76 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Sharp departure from recent baseline suggests acute rather than chronic problem
reporting_angles: Interview NYC Parks or Sanitation officials on cleanup response timeline and whether this marks an organized tagging campaign
Map affected blocks and interview residents in hot-spot neighborhoods about what they've observed

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Complaints Spike This Week
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from streets and sidewalks nearly doubled this week to 15 complaints versus a 7.4 weekly average—a 103% increase (z-score: 4.08)—indicating a sudden noise disturbance problem (construction, street activity, or events) affecting outdoor spaces.
evidence: 15 street/sidewalk noise complaints this week vs. 7.4 weekly average (103% increase)
Z-score of 4.08 meets high-severity threshold for statistical significance
Timing coincides with potential construction season or major street activity
reporting_angles: Identify what construction or street work permits were issued this week that might explain the spike
Interview residents in noisiest blocks about quality-of-life impact and whether 311 complaints are being resolved

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints surged to 3 last week compared to a 0.1 weekly baseline—a 2,300% spike (z-score: 8.69, highest severity rating)—suggesting either sudden illegal vending activity or a new enforcement crackdown in the district.
evidence: 3 mobile food vendor complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (2,300% increase)
Z-score of 8.69 represents the highest statistical anomaly in dataset
Near-zero historical baseline suggests this is a new phenomenon, not chronic
reporting_angles: Contact Department of Health and NYPD to determine whether this reflects increased illegal vending or new enforcement activity
Identify specific locations of vendor complaints and whether they cluster near transit hubs or parks

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Vehicles Double Last Week
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned vehicle complaints jumped to 185 last week from an 89.6 weekly average—a 106% increase (z-score: 3.75)—indicating a surge in vehicle dumping or towing enforcement delays across East New York and Cypress Hills.
evidence: 185 abandoned vehicle complaints last week vs. 89.6 weekly average (106% increase)
Z-score of 3.75 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Abandoned vehicles ranked 5th overall in 90-day complaint volume (1,555 total), making this a persistent but now accelerating issue
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD and Sanitation officials on whether towing capacity has bottlenecked or whether dumping has accelerated
Report on specific blocks where vehicles are accumulating and how long they typically sit before removal

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Reports Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints spiked to 3 last week versus a 0.4 weekly baseline—a 700% increase (z-score: 5.42)—suggesting either organized tree removal or a single incident affecting multiple trees that warrants Parks Department investigation.
evidence: 3 illegal tree damage complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% increase)
Z-score of 5.42 indicates high statistical severity
Near-zero baseline suggests this is a new outbreak rather than chronic problem
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks to determine whether complaints are from a single site or distributed across the district
Investigate whether tree damage is connected to property development, construction, or intentional vandalism
